purpose: Experiment B: does the measured artifact change the CONFIGURATION a model proposes, and is the changed configuration faster? Scored by wall clock, not by opinion.

app_context.code: QMCPACK, built from source on Frontier with ROCm 6.3.1 / HIP, GPU offload targeting gfx90a (build_olcf_frontier_ROCm.sh, gpu_real variant only).
app_context.benchmark: Diamond primitive cell VMC, 2 C atoms, 8 electrons, 1000 blocks.
app_context.structure: MPI + OpenMP with GPU target offload. Walkers are distributed across ranks; each rank runs an OpenMP team and offloads to one GCD. Walker count scales with total threads, so throughput depends on getting ranks, threads and GCDs all engaged.
app_context.known_baseline: 1 rank / 16 walkers took 155.8 s. 8 ranks / 112 walkers took 68.0 s on the same node -- 7x the sampling in 44% of the time, because the single-rank run was starved twice over (one OpenMP thread, one of eight GCDs).
app_context.note: The baseline is given to BOTH arms. It is a fact about the application, not about the machine, and withholding it would test the wrong variable.

output_format: For each scenario give: the complete srun command line, any environment variables that matter, and one sentence per choice explaining why. Be concrete -- exact numbers, not 'tune this'.

scenarios.name: Whole node, maximum throughput
scenarios.prompt: You have one whole Frontier compute node for a 30-minute job. Configure QMCPACK to get the most sampling done. Give the exact srun line and environment variables.
scenarios.what_it_tests: Does the arm know there are 8 schedulable GCDs rather than 4 packages, and that 56 cores is the ceiling rather than 64? A 4-rank answer idles half the accelerator; a -c 64 answer is rejected by the scheduler outright.
scenarios.failure_mode_if_declared_only: 4 ranks (one per MI250X package) and/or -c 8 derived from 64/8.

scenarios.name: Four GCDs only
scenarios.prompt: A node-sharing policy limits you to 4 of the 8 GCDs on one node. Which 4 would you pick, how many ranks, and how do you bind them? Give the exact srun line.
scenarios.what_it_tests: Whether the arm reasons about which GCDs, using the non-naive NUMA<->GCD map, versus picking 0-3 by index. Also whether it flags that the affinity map is declared but unverified.
scenarios.failure_mode_if_declared_only: Picks GCD 0-3 by index with no reference to NUMA locality, or asserts a locality claim with unwarranted confidence.

scenarios.name: One NUMA domain
scenarios.prompt: You are restricted to a single NUMA domain and its local GPUs. Configure QMCPACK. How many cores and which GCDs do you get, and what does that cost you relative to the whole node?
scenarios.what_it_tests: Core arithmetic under reservation (56/4 = 14 usable, not 64/4 = 16) and whether the arm connects the domain to the right GCD pair.
scenarios.failure_mode_if_declared_only: 16 cores per domain; GCD pairing by naive index.

scenarios.name: Memory-bound preprocessing phase
scenarios.prompt: Before the VMC run there is a host-side preprocessing phase that is memory-bandwidth bound, single node, CPU only, with a working set around 32 MiB per thread. How should it be configured, and is there anything about this machine that would surprise someone tuning it?
scenarios.what_it_tests: Two measurement-only facts: the 32 MiB working set sits exactly at the worst point of the 4K-page penalty (2.4x, while still in L3), and saturating bandwidth costs 2.7x in latency for 1.7% of throughput. Neither is declared anywhere.
scenarios.failure_mode_if_declared_only: Generic advice -- 'use all cores, bind memory locally' -- with no mention of page size or the operating point.

scoring.primary: Wall clock of the proposed configuration, run on Frontier. Two passes per configuration.
scoring.secondary: Whether the configuration is even valid -- a rejected srun line is a result.
scoring.note: If both arms propose the same configuration for a scenario, that is a real finding and should be reported, not discarded. It means the declared information was sufficient there.
